sections.heading: Turn Insights into Impact with AI-Powered Workflows
sections.body: Guided by ongoing partner input, our connected workflows continuously evolve to meet the needs of different teams across campus—supporting the day-to-day realities of advisors, faculty, student success leaders, and administrators. Connected workflows, enriched by actionable insights and institution-specific AI assistance, are integrated directly into daily campus operations to help teams take timely, effective, and coordinated action. Now, every advisor, faculty member, and leader can move seamlessly from insight to impact.

sections.heading: What Makes Civitas Learning Workflows Unique?
bullets: Embedded Insights: Surface real-time, student-specific insights, alerts, and AI-generated recommendations in the tools your teams already use—so they can intervene faster and with greater precision.

AI-Powered Collaboration: AI assistants help teams create notes, build student groups, and document interactions in seconds—so staff stay focused on students, while everything stays in one place to keep teams aligned and accountable.

Integrated Outreach: Drive timely engagement with built-in communication tools—nudges, personalized emails, SMS, and appointment reminders. AI assistants help craft outreach and suggest next steps, while advisors decide what happens next.

sections.heading: Workflow Features that Power Better Student Outcomes
bullets: Real-Time Academic Alerts & Case Management: Automatically flag at-risk students using predictive models built for your institution. Surface academic alerts in the context of other insights to ensure students get the right support at the right time. Track resolution, follow-up, and student progress in one place.

Collaborative Notes & Cross-Team Visibility: Capture advising session notes instantly—with AI auto-summarization, so your staff stays focused on students. Share and access holistic student records, making it easy for faculty, advisors, and support staff to coordinate care.

Integrated Communication Tools: Launch targeted outreach and nudge campaigns using student data filters to enhance engagement. Send personalized emails and texts based on student risk, status, or milestone—ensuring the right message reaches the right student, every time.

Dynamic Student Lists: Create, update, and share lists for targeted engagement, such as outreach to students at risk for stopping out, those nearing completion, or those in need of registration nudges. Make sure every message reaches the right student, with the right context, from the right voice.
Proactive Planning & Scheduling: Enable students to build degree roadmaps, select optimal course schedules, and receive structured guidance—all seamlessly connected to advisor workflows.

sections.heading: Benefits for Every Campus Team
bullets: For Leaders: Govern campus-wide engagement strategies with visibility into team actions, case statuses, and student touchpoints—so strategy stays grounded in people, not just dashboards. Measure workflow efficiency and student impact—adjust and scale best practices institution-wide.

For Student-Facing Teams: Reduce manual workload and administrative burden—freeing up time to focus on meaningful student interactions. Act earlier and more effectively with at-a-glance student risk alerts, real-time updates, and automated communication tools.
For Students: Get timely support and guidance, without having to seek it out. Enjoy a seamless experience, from receiving alerts to scheduling appointments—all personalized to their unique needs.

name: Strategic Enrollment & Retention Software
headline: Make your number. Then keep it.
sub: You are judged on the fall census, and again on spring retention. Every admit gets two scores in the CRM your counselors already open: will they enroll, and will they still be here in year two.

sections.heading: What a VP of Enrollment gets
bullets: Hit the census number: Two scores on every admit, in the CRM your counselors already open, so the team works the list from the top and the agent works the rest.
Stop the melt: The admit who goes quiet surfaces the day it happens, with the outreach drafted and the follow-up booked.
Register the students you already have: Continuing students who have not registered by week two, named, with the hold identified. SUNY Broome raised registration 3.7%.
Keep the class you recruited: Second-year persistence reported next to yield, so you find out whether the class you built actually stays.

sections.heading: See which admits will enroll, and which will still be here in year two
sections.body: Two predictions from a model trained on your own admit and enrollment history, not on sector averages: likelihood to enroll, and likelihood to persist into year two. A yield decision that fills the class with students who leave raises this year's census and next year's attrition, so the platform reports both numbers together.

image.alt: Student outcome predictions for an admitted class

sections.heading: Work the melt list before the deposit deadline passes
sections.body: Deposited students who have gone quiet are scored daily and ranked, so a counselor opens the day with the twenty names that matter rather than the whole file. The outreach is drafted and the follow-up is booked, which is what makes proactive contact survive a busy July.

image.alt: Prioritized outreach list for admitted students

sections.heading: Clear the registration holds that cost you the spring number
sections.body: Continuing students who have not registered by week two of open registration are found by name, with the hold that is stopping them identified, so the conversation starts from the fix. SUNY Broome raised registration 3.7% by working that list.

image.alt: Student registration and schedule builder

sections.heading: Open the sections that hold the class
sections.body: Section-level analytics show which sections are filling fastest and which modalities, days, and times students actually pick, and forecast demand for the next term. A student who cannot get a required seat is an enrollment problem before it is an academic one.

image.alt: Real-time section fill and course demand

sections.heading: Find the gateway course that costs you next year's returning class
sections.body: Some courses quietly remove students from the institution. Course-level analysis shows which ones reduce persistence for which populations, so you can put tutoring or supplemental instruction where it changes the second-year number instead of spreading it evenly.

image.alt: Course impact on persistence and completion

sections.heading: The rule has changed. Graduate earnings now decide loan eligibility.
sections.body: Under the Department of Education's earnings accountability framework, finalized in 2026 and effective July 2027, every Title IV-eligible degree program is measured against what its graduates earn. A program whose graduates repeatedly earn less than working adults with only a high school diploma loses federal loan eligibility. The determination arrives years after the students it describes enrolled. By then the only options are to close the program or absorb the loss. The career module gives deans and provosts the same view the Department will have, program by program, years earlier.

sections.heading: A diagnostic, not an autopsy
sections.body: Employment data arrives after graduation, when nothing can be done. The career readiness index is a real-time view of each student's progress toward a career: internships, experiential learning, career programming, mentorship, and résumé work, alongside persistence and grades. Think of it as a degree plan for career readiness. A student can carry a 3.4 GPA and still be unprepared for the job market. The index shows that in the sophomore year, not in a wage record four years after commencement.

image.alt: Post-Graduation Outcomes: matched graduates, employment within 6 and 12 months, major-aligned careers, time to first job, current salary, and salary growth, with employment rate by graduation year

sections.heading: Every student and every graduate, over years. Not a first-destination survey.
sections.body: A first-destination survey reaches the graduates who answer, six months out, once. The career module maps the whole student body while they are enrolled and every alumni cohort after they leave, year over year, by program and by student group. That is the same longitudinal view the Department of Education uses for the earnings test, and it is the only way to see whether a curriculum change made in 2026 moved the earnings of the class of 2030. Career readiness while enrolled, outcomes after, one record per student from first term to fifth year out.

image.alt: Outcomes by major: graduates, employment at 6 and 12 months, major alignment, stayed local, months to job, current salary, and salary growth for every program

sections.heading: A scoreboard for every dean
sections.body: Each degree program gets one page: enrollment, engagement, persistence, graduation, career readiness, and, where your state wage data allows, graduate earnings against the federal threshold. Deans and chairs see which programs are clear, which are close, and which need a curriculum change, an internship pipeline, or a hard conversation. The same page answers the accreditor, the state, and the board.

image.alt: One program selected: 622 nursing graduates, 92% employed within 12 months, $75,852 average current salary, employment rate by graduation year

sections.heading: Find the students who are not career ready, while there is time
sections.body: Dynamic student groups update as data changes. The junior in a business program with no internship, no career center visit, and a persistence score that dropped this term is on a list by Monday. Career services, the advisor, and the department see the same list and the same plan. Outreach goes to the students who need it, not to everyone.

image.alt: Dynamic student groups for targeted career outreach

sections.heading: Measure which career programs move persistence and earnings
sections.body: Internships, alumni mentoring, applied learning courses, career coaching: institutions offer all of them and rarely know which ones work for which students. Every career program is measured against a matched comparison group on persistence, completion, and later earnings, by student group. UT San Antonio found statistically significant retention gains for students who met with career consultants or received mentorship. The budget follows the evidence.
